commits.message:
feat(drafts): full-reparse backfill so a parser improvement reaches the existing backlog

Verified live after #8/#9 deployed: backfill_signature_company_fill's
own dry_run reported 0 fillable drafts, because it only ever reuses
whatever signature was already STORED on a draft -- it can't benefit
from a signature-PARSER improvement (the relay_from_block detector)
shipped after that draft was first intake'd. The stored signature for
the whole PROHIRES POWERHOUSE backlog still says company_not_detected;
it was never re-parsed.

Adds backfill_full_reparse(): re-runs the full deterministic pipeline
(parse_email_business_records, parse_email_signature,
apply_learned_signature_patterns, apply_signature_company_fill) from
each draft's own stored raw text, same as live intake, deliberately
MINUS the LLM fallback -- a bulk operation over the whole backlog is
not the place for per-draft LLM calls under the standing
deterministic-first cost policy. Skips any draft with a recorded
reviewer/recruiter correction so a human's prior edit is never
silently discarded by the re-parse. dry_run=True by default.

Exposed as POST /drafts/backfill/full-reparse (drafts:publish),
alongside the existing backfill/signature-company-fill endpoint.

Bug caught before shipping: the first draft of this query selected
d.payload/d.metadata but not d.status, so was_requires_review always
read as False and moved_out_of_review_count could never populate --
fixed by selecting d.status and deriving it from that.

3 new tests in scripts/hermes-850-signature-company-fill-check.py,
using the real YARDI CONSULTANT production text end-to-end (recovers
both the company via the new signature detector AND collapses the
false 5-record split back to 1), plus dry-run and human-correction
guards.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

test: stop asserting membership in the capped backfill result lists

CI failure on the previous push: draft_id was correctly in
changed_draft_ids but the test asserted it must also be in
moved_out_of_review_ids and that failed. Both lists are populated in
the same single pass over the (unlimited, ORDER BY created_at) query
result and truncated to [:50] for the API response -- by the time this
script runs, the shared CI database already holds many other
draft_job_requirement rows from every earlier check script in the same
job, so a list built that way is not a reliable thing for a test to
assert membership in. Switched all three new tests to check the
actually-persisted draft state via get_draft_object instead, which is
what the fix is actually supposed to produce and isn't affected by how
many other rows happen to exist in the shared test database.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

test: make the full-reparse test diagnostic instead of guessing further

CI failure moved from list-membership (fixed last commit) to the
status assertion itself: draft stayed 'needs_review' after a real
apply. Reordering the checks (signature method -> record_count ->
company -> confidence -> requires_review -> status) so the next CI
failure, if any, points directly at which stage of the pipeline
diverges from the already-verified-live behavior, instead of only
seeing the final downstream symptom.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

test: give the full-reparse fixture an explicit Required Skills: label

Root cause of the previous failure, now that the diagnostic pointed
right at it: not a production bug -- my own shortened test fixture
dropped the "SQL scripting" mention the original real email had, so
the generic taxonomy-driven skill match found nothing and
required_skills_not_identified correctly fired (confidence 0.62, not
0.92). The parser was right; the fixture was incomplete. Fixed by
adding an explicit "Required Skills:" label instead of depending on
which taxonomy keywords happen to appear incidentally in prose --
deterministic and independent of the taxonomy's current contents.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
